summary: 1926 60-foot Aermotor fire tower on Broad Mountain, Blythe Township, Pennsylvania; closed by 2013 and found fenced in 2021; NHLR-registered 2004.

facts.design: 60-foot steel Aermotor tower with 7x7 observation cab
facts.status_note: Last account (July 2021) describes it as out of use and enclosed by a fence; no later source was read.

access.note: Closed by 2013 for aging and vandalism; a 2021 visitor found it fenced off. No current visiting rules documented.

News report of August 25, 2013: closed due to aging and vandalism; upkeep short of budget and maintenance staff

resolved_conflicts.explanation: NHLR says the tower is 'just south of' Weiser State Forest, while Forest Lookouts files it under Weiser State Forest. The story uses NHLR's wording.
NHLR names the Pennsylvania Bureau of Forestry as administrator and says the land is owned by Blythe Township. Both are reported; the sources do not say how the arrangement works in practice.

sources.title: An Unexpected Hike To The Silver Creek Fire Tower In Locust Lake State Park

notes_for_editor: Brief checked: 1926 build, 2004 registration, agency and 18.3 m (60 ft) height all match the sources; no corrections. Access changed from unknown to closed on the 2013 news report and 2021 visitor account. The mid-1940s storm year is not given, so no event was recorded for it. The 2013 closure comes from one news report quoted by Forest Lookouts. The blog's 'about 20 years' is a visitor's estimate. The ArcGIS map series gave no readable text, and the DCNR Weiser history page did not mention the tower. A 2023 Locust Lake State Park Facebook hike listing appeared in search, but its page text was not readable, so it is not cited. Current condition is unverified. No photos added.
